title: Annotatio V §.XI close: Jn 6:54 spiritual souls’ eating; stop before §.XII Lutheran testimonia
pass_a_gloss: For how (asks the Author near the end of Paragraph XIX, about to swell Ignoratio Elenchi with petitio principii) does incorruption remain in flesh fed and sustained by the Lord’s body and blood as by the tree of life? But if the Author wants the genuine cause of incorruptibility of bodies that worthily received the Eucharist and whence they obtained resurrection hope, let him learn it from Christ’s own mouth: it is not corporal Eating of Christ’s body, but Spiritual Eating of souls — of which alone, on the Author’s own hypothesis, Christ speaks in John 6: Who eats my Flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life — namely as to the body, not as to the soul — for I will raise him up on the last day, v. 54.
pass_b_english: Near §.XIX’s end the Author asks how flesh stays incorrupt if fed by the Lord’s body and blood as by the tree of life — stacking petitio principii on Ignoratio Elenchi.

The real cause, from Christ’s mouth, is not corporal eating but Spiritual eating of souls alone (Jn 6:54: eat my Flesh, drink my blood — eternal life as to the body; I will raise him). Stop §.XI before §.XII.
source_text: Quomodo enim (quærit Autor circa finem Paragraphi XIX, Elenchi Ignorationem petitione principii adaucturus) incorruptio maneat caro, quæ à corpore Domini & sanguine, velut ab arbore vitæ, alitur & sustentatur? Quodsi verò Auctor genuinam causam Incorruptibilitatis corporum eorum, quæ dignè Eucharistiam perceperunt, & unde resurrectionis spem indepta sint, cognoscere cupit, ex ipsius Christi ore istud intelligat, non corporalem corporis Christi Manducationem, eam esse, sed Spiritualem Animarum, de qua, & quidem sola, ex hypothesi Autoris, ita Christus Joh. 6. Qui manducat Carnem meam & bibit sanguinem meum, hoc ipso habet vitam æternam, putà quà corpus, non quà animam, namque suscitabo eum in die novissimo, vers. 54.
